title: Reba McEntire + Miranda Lambert Are VERY Different in One Way: 'I Was Shocked' - NewsBreak
text:
By Carena Liptak ,
8 hours ago Jason Kempin (2), Getty Images They’re both country music traditionalists who have a love of rodeos and have spent a lot of time in Texas. But Reba McEntire and Miranda Lambert are very different in at least one key way.
In a new interview with Esquire , McEntire revealed that she and Lambert have very different attitudes toward winning awards. Lambert, she says, is a “share the wealth” kind of person, while McEntire admits she’s always hoping to win — no matter how many times she’s already been recognized in a category.
“I’m very competitive,” McEntire admits. “I get a No. 1 record, I want another No. 1 record. I win an award, I want another one.”
McEntire assumed her fellow country stars all felt the same way, which is why she was so shocked over a conversation she and Lambert had backstage at an awards show one year.
“I’ll never forget Miranda Lambert coming up to me when she was nominated for Female Vocalist of the Year after she’d already won it, and I said, ‘Good luck, Miranda,'” McEntire recounts. “She said, ‘Oh, I already won, it’s time for somebody else.'”
“What person lets that come out of their mouth? I was shocked,” she goes on to say. “I thought everybody was just like me.”
Miranda Lambert + Reba McEntire Are In Sync Where it Counts (Music!) All competition aside, Lambert and McEntire have bonded over their status as country music flame-keepers, and the sacred task of preserving the genre and passing it down into the hands of a new generation of women.
Read More : Miranda, Reba + Lainey’s Collab: “Trailblazer” Lyrics Are Personal
Together with Lainey Wilson , they recorded a song on that theme titled “Trailblazer,” which they debuted at this year’s ACM Awards.
Reba McEntire Gets Engaged to Rex Linn The big non-musical news in McEntire’s life is that she recently got engaged to actor Rex Lin, whom she’s been dating since 2020.
Read More : Reba + Rex Are Engaged!
The news slipped out on the red carpet at the Emmy Awards on Sunday night (Sept. 14). An E! News reporter referred to them as fiancés, and they later confirmed the happy news to People .
That engagement has been brewing for quite a while.
All the way back in 2023, McEntire said she was open to the idea of marrying Linn and that it was totally up to him to decide if that was something he wanted to do.
The Top 20 Reba McEntire Songs, Ranked Gallery Credit: Billy Dukes/Carena Liptak MCA Records No. 20: "How Blue" This early-career release from 1984 spotlights McEntire's simple, traditional country roots. Not only that, but the song has staying power: In 2006, the singer revisited "How Blue" as a duet with Dolly Parton during an episode of CMT Giants . MCA Nashville No. 19: "He Gets That From Me" This tender 2004 single earned McEntire a Top 10 country radio hit, but its storytelling is what truly makes "He Gets That From Me" special. The song is about a mom raising her son on her own after the boy's father dies and her bittersweet experience of seeing all the ways in which her child resembles his late dad. MCA Nashville No. 18: "Somebody Should Leave" McEntire's 1984 My Kind of Country album was all about embracing a traditional sound, and "Somebody Should Leave" — a song about a marriage gone sour — was penned by country songwriting legend Harlan Howard. MCA Nashville No. 17: "For My Broken Heart" This No. 1 country hit is also the title track of the first album McEntire released after a plane crash killed several members of her band and crew in March 1991. "For My Broken Heart" works as a song about a failed relationship, but the lyric " I guess the world didn't stop for my broken heart " also offers some perspective into the singer's journey through grief after losing her friends in the tragedy. Big Machine No. 16: "Back to God" McEntire has never shied away from her strong Christian faith in her music. Her Sing It Now: Songs of Faith & Hope gospel album celebrates her relationship with her faith, and "Back to God" — one of the album's original songs — is a rousing call to action for believers everywhere. MCA Records No. 15: "She Thinks His Name Was John" McEntire put her finger on the pulse of a worldwide tragedy when she released "She Thinks His Name Was John" in 1994, the same year that AIDS officially became the leading cause of death in Americans aged 25-44. This song's lyrics tell the story of a woman dying from AIDS after contracting HIV from a one-night stand with a stranger. Co-writer Sandy Knox was inspired to write this ballad after losing her brother to this devastating illness. YouTube No. 14: "You Lie" Some of McEntire's biggest hits were cover songs that she made her own, including "You Lie." This song was originally recorded in the late '80s by Cee Cee Chapman, but it made an even bigger impact when McEntire released it in 1990 as the lead single off her Rumor Has It album. "You Lie" was McEntire's 14th No. 1 country hit. Starstruck Records/Valory Music Co. No. 13: "Consider Me Gone" Some artists peak within their first couple album cycles, but this empowering breakup anthem proved McEntire's longevity. Released in 2009 as a single off her Keep on Loving You album, "Consider Me Gone" was McEntire's 24th career No. 1 hit and also became her longest-running No. 1, staying at the top of the chart for four weeks. MCA Nashville/Arista Records No. 12: "If You See Him/If You See Her" (with Brooks & Dunn) McEntire's friendship with the guys of Brooks & Dunn is long and well-documented. Fans might even have her to thank for the duo's reunion after their 2009 breakup, when she convinced them to return to the stage with her for a joint Las Vegas residency. They've also collaborated on a couple of duets, including this No. 1 country hit from 1998. Rockin' R Records No. 11: "Seven Minutes in Heaven" "Seven Minutes in Heaven" isn't the only song McEntire has released inspired by her mom, Jacqueline. The two were very close, and Mama McEntire was a massive influence on her superstar daughter's career. But this song is our favorite, for an emotional reason.
It was released after Jacqueline died in March 2020, and poses a hypothetical: What would this mother-daughter duo talk about, if McEntire could take a quick trip up to Heaven to visit her mom? The song is enough of a tear-jerker all on its own, but the music video takes it over the top. MCA Nashville No. 10: "Why Haven't I Heard From You" Co-written by one of McEntire's closest and longest-running songwriter connections, Sandy Knox, "Why Haven't I Heard From You" only made it as far as No. 5 on the charts. But charts aren't everything, and this personality-packed country twanger became a staple of McEntire's live show and arguably one of the most fun-to-sing-along-to songs she's ever released. MCA Nashville 9. "Does He Love You" Linda Davis released her first singles in 1988 on Capitol Records. However, it wasn’t until her 1993 appearance on McEntire’s "Does He Love You" that she would finally see massive success. The collaboration earned a CMA award and a Grammy, while Davis enjoyed greater exposure touring with McEntire's live show. Davis would later revel in the success of her daughter, Lady A's Hillary Scott. Mercury 8. "Can't Even Get the Blues'" Reba McEntire was not an overnight success. "Can’t Even Get the Blues" became her first No. 1 single in 1982 after 16 modest single record releases. The song from 1981's Unlimited album launched McEntire into the most successful period of her career. MCA Nashville 7. "The Night the Lights Went Out in Georgia" McEntire scored a major hit with her dynamic cover version of Vicki Lawrence's 1972 hit Southern gothic tale of small town intrigue that leads to murder. Her version of "The Night the Lights Went Out in Georgia" reached No. 12 in 1992. Valory Music Group 6. "Turn on the Radio" "Turn on the Radio" was quite an accomplishment for McEntire. At the time the song was released, she was 55, and as it soared up the charts, it proved that the music veteran could still compete with the young stars of the day. The smash hit was her 60th Top 10 single on the country charts, making her the first female country artist in history to achieve that many Top 10s. When the song reached the top, it became her 25th No. 1 song, tying Dolly Parton for the most No. 1s by a female country artist ever. MCA Nashville 5. "The Greatest Man I Never Knew" Like many of her hit songs, McEntire sings "The Greatest Man I Never Knew" like she wrote it. However, the somber tune was co-penned by Layng Martine, Jr. and Richard Leigh, the same man who wrote "Don’t It Make My Brown Eyes Blue" for Crystal Gayle. McEntire always explained in concert that the story in the song was very close to the relationship that she had with her own father. This 1992 classic is a must-have on our list of the best Reba McEntire songs. MCA Nashville 4. "Whoever's in New England" Although McEntire had already racked up four No. 1 hits by the time "Whoever’s in New England" came along, the song was considered a career-changing milestone. In addition to having a successful power ballad on radio for the first time, she released a video which showcased her acting skills and served as a foreshadow to the style of videos that she would later produce for some of her biggest hits. In 1986, the song won McEntire her first Grammy for Female Vocalist and the CMA gave her the top honor of Entertainer of the Year. 3. "Is There Life Out There" In 1992, McEntire seemed to keep raising the bar for her own career. Concert productions were becoming more theatrical, television appearances were increasing and music videos were becoming more like mini-movies. "Is There Life Out There" was accompanied by a video that was so long that video outlets were reluctant to play it. In the end, the song was turned into a made-for-TV movie and inspired many women to complete their education. The motivational single stayed at No. 1 for two solid weeks! MCA Nashville 2. "Fancy" Bobbie Gentry, the singer of 1967’s "Ode to Billie Joe," wrote and recorded the original version of "Fancy" in 1969. Reba McEntire slipped on a red dress and brought "Fancy" up the charts in 1991. Although the single only peaked at No. 8, the song is easily considered one of Reba McEntire’s signature songs and a shoo-in for this list. MCA Nashville 1. "I'm a Survivor" In 2001, after conquering Broadway in Annie Get Your Gun, McEntire continued to branch out in her entertainment empire by starring in her own successful sitcom, Reba . "I’m a Survivor" was an appropriate pick for the show’s theme song. The tune’s inspirational message, which represents the true spirit of this positive role model, is just one of the reason’s we’ve selected it as our No. 1 Reba McEntire song of all time.
